title: Comprehensive care at the community health center - Health in the center
summary:
People who live in so-called hotspot districts, i.e. in socially and structurally disadvantaged neighbourhoods, are also more frequently exposed to particular physical, psychological and social challenges than the general population. They therefore need specifically coordinated healthcare, the complexity of which has not yet been taken into account in current standard care.

The NAVIGATION project team wants to develop a specific care model for this population group and test it in a study. The model centres on contacting those affected directly in their living environment, offering support and working with them to find solutions that are compatible with everyday life in dealing with their illnesses. This is done by specially trained community health nurses and staff from the primary care centres involved. Following an initial needs analysis, treatment planning is tailored to the individual. They are then implemented with the digital support of doctors and nurses as required. In addition, those affected can take advantage of tailored individual counselling and participatory group offers. 

The effectiveness of the model will be scientifically analysed on the basis of questionnaires. At the same time, the cost development of the new form of care compared to the current standard care will be examined on the basis of health economic analyses. As part of a process evaluation, the procedures will be assessed in order to determine, for example, success factors or barriers to implementation.

If the new care model proves successful, it will improve healthcare provision of people from socially and structurally disadvantaged regions. At the same time, optimised care planning reduces costs in the healthcare system. In this way, health inequalities in disadvantaged regions can be reduced in the long term.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Intervention group (individual):
Patients capable of giving consent who live in the service area of the respective health centre, have at least one chronic illness and at least one social problem and are covered by statutory health insurance.

Intervention group at social area level, control group:
Patients capable of giving consent who live in the health centre's service area (intervention group at social area level) or live in neighbourhoods with a similar population composition (pre-selection, control group)
Exclusion criteria:
Patients under guardianship in the area of health care
